issues.body: `_worker_pulls_for_issue` calls `api.paginate` on `matching-refs` and treats the resulting set as complete. The prefix can match an unbounded number of leftover/re-dispatched attempt refs; it is not an exact single-object lookup. If a matching ref is deleted while that listing is paged, later rows can shift across the cursor boundary just as they can in the repo-wide pull walk. The live PR's ref can therefore be absent from this result while the PR is simultaneously skipped by `_pulls`, causing the union to contain neither row and permitting the claim to be reaped. The comments' assertion that this read is not a population walk / cannot be page-skipped, and the stated request bound, are consequently false. The added tests use `_RefListingAPI`, which returns one preassembled list and cannot simulate pagination or a between-page mutation, so they do not detect this failure.
issues.fix_hint: Use an evidence path whose completeness does not depend on enumerating a mutable set of matching refs (for example, derive and directly query a bounded set of authoritative candidate heads, or use a server-side query with a sound completeness argument). Add an end-to-end test that models more than one page and deletes a preceding ref between page reads, then prove the live worker PR still retains the lease. If no complete keyed witness is available, defer rather than treating an enumerated empty/partial ref set as proof of absence.
issues.title: The keyed witness still relies on a shiftable paginated ref listing

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new corroborating read is fail-closed on API errors and validates returned pull rows, but it does not establish the claimed independent absence proof: its first stage is itself a paginated population walk over every matching worker ref. With enough retained/re-dispatched refs, the same page-boundary deletion race can omit the ref carrying the live PR. The tests only exercise a single in-memory page and therefore do not cover the marquee race at this new evidence path.
